content.title: Kimi Antonelli Wins First Formula 1 Race at Chinese Grand Prix
content.text: Kimi Antonelli controlled the Chinese Grand Prix to pick up his maiden victory in Formula 1 as Mercedes dominated once more, while Lewis Hamilton returned to the podium, and McLaren endured a nightmare. Autoweek rounds up the main talking points from Shanghai.Antonelli delivers on Mercedes faithMercedes has long had unwavering faith in Kimi Antonelli’s abilities, signing him as a young teenager, putting him in Formula 2 with little experience, and then promoting him straight to Formula 1 to the factory team. Last year was a learning season, and there were the expected pitfalls and mistakes, perhaps one or two more than both driver and team would have liked. This was the season to kick on, and kick on Antonelli has. George Russell was briefly delayed by the fast-starting Ferraris, but had recovered to second by the time the safety car was deployed for Lance Stroll’s stricken Aston Martin. At the restart while Antonelli surged clear Russell struggled for grip and fell behind both Ferraris; while Russell eventually reclaimed second by the time he had done so Antonelli had established an insurmountable buffer. A late lock-up into the hairpin provided a scare but it was the only minor blemish as Antonelli claimed a well-deserved maiden win. At the age of 19 he is the second-youngest winner in history, and of the current grid only Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen took fewer grands prix to find the top step of the podium. Peter Fox//Getty ImagesKimi Antonelli and his father, Marco Antonelli.Advertisement - Continue Reading Below“Right from his days in karting, we have known that he has all the talent necessary to develop into a Grand Prix winner,” said Mercedes boss Toto Wolff. “His family, along with the team, have done a brilliant job nurturing that talent and today shows that. There have been so many doubters writing him off, saying it was too early, that he doesn't have the composure necessary, and Kimi has proven them all wrong. This is just the start for him; he will keep his feet on the ground and keep working hard but he can definitely enjoy himself this evening.”“There have been so many doubters writing him off, saying it was too early, that he doesn't have the composure necessary, and Kimi has proven them all wrong.”Antonelli was emotional in the aftermath of the win as he strived to take in the enormity of his accomplishment. “I’m super, super happy,” he said. “It’s such an incredible day and very grateful for achieving my first win. The team did an incredible job. The car is super quick and it’s allowing us to fight for wins. I’m really happy because they also helped me to achieve one of my big dreams. Yeah, just super, super happy.”Hamilton finally takes Ferrari podiumIt’s been a long time coming, and he had to properly fight for it, but Lewis Hamilton claimed his first grand prix podium in Ferrari colors in Shanghai. Hamilton, who has taken Sprint Race podiums with Ferrari, embarked in a fierce scrap against team-mate Charles Leclerc, but the pair kept it clean while swapping positions on several occasions. The fight was eventually settled in favor of Hamilton, who took the record-extending 203rdpodium of his career, and first since Las Vegas 2024. Kym Illman//Getty ImagesLewis Hamilton.“I started this voyage and this dream of moving to Ferrari and being on the top step with them, and this podium has taken longer than I had hoped,” Hamilton said. “After a difficult year last year, to be able to be a part of developing with them, working with them over the past year, gives me huge pride and it’s such a privilege to be a part of this brand. They provided us a really solid car.”Advertisement - Continue Reading BelowHamilton agreed that a victory is “more in sight than ever before” and “last year it couldn’t have been further from view,” but cautioned that Ferrari faces a deficit to pacesetters Mercedes. “In the race trim I think they’ve got four or five tenths on us at the moment,” Hamilton said. “That’s a huge step to pick up, both in downforce and efficiency and also power. That’s a huge upgrade that we need to push for. But I really do believe in everyone back in Maranello and that it’s not an impossible feat to overcome.”Shellshocked McLaren suffers double pre-race failureFormula 1 teams have been gradually encountering glitches and setbacks under the new regulations but reigning champions McLaren didn’t even manage to make the start with either car in China. An electrical issue was detected on Lando Norris’ car an hour before the pit lane opened and he didn’t even make it out of the garage, while Oscar Piastri’s car was wheeled off the grid shortly before the start because of a different electrical problem. The pair had been due to start from fifth and sixth respectively but instead watched on from the garage as McLaren endured its first double Did Not Start since the Indianapolis tire debacle in 2005. NurPhoto//Getty Images“It’s disappointing to come such a long way and put in so much effort, not just me but the whole team, and to not start the race,” said Norris, who suffered the first non-start of his career.For Piastri it marked his second successive failure to start a race, off the back of his pre-grid accident in Melbourne.“While this is never what we want to happen, this is just sometimes how it goes in racing,” Piastri said. “Even more frustrating is missing out on another race distance, as we know that time on track is critical in learning how to get the most out of this era of cars.”“It’s disappointing to come such a long way and put in so much effort, not just me but the whole team, and to not start the race.”Advertisement - Continue Reading BelowNorris and Piastri were two of four drivers who failed to even make the start, with Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto and Williams’ Alex Albon both marooned pre-race due to mechanical woes. Verstappen also exits, as does AlonsoRed Bull endured a troubled weekend in Shanghai, with the RB22 off the pace, while Verstappen struggled for balance and as a knock-on effect suffered high tire graining, too, having encountered yet another terrible start. Verstappen was only on course for a low-key sixth place when he encountered an ERS cooling problem in the closing stages and brought the car back to retirement. Mark Thompson//Getty ImagesMax Verstappen retiring.“We faced the same problems that we had in Melbourne: we had a lot of degradation and were still struggling with the pace and the grip,” Verstappen said. “We tried a different procedure to help with the start, had a similar issue, and lost quite a few positions at the beginning, ending up at the back of the grid. There are quite a few things we need to go away and analyze and learn from in order to improve our overall performance of the car. It is not where we want to be.”Aston Martin’s woes continued as, despite Honda implementing countermeasures, the vibrations from the car were so excessive that Fernando Alonso was forced to retire. Alonso made a typically combative start, briefly creeping into the top 10, but the limitations of the car meant he was powerless to prevent rapidly sliding back down the order. TV footage showed Alonso regularly removing his hands from the steering wheel due to the force of the vibrations, and after 32 laps he called it a day.“From about lap 20 I was struggling with the vibration levels, and we were already one lap down, so in the end we decided to retire the car,” Alonso said. “The vibrations seemed worse today than on any other day of the weekend, so we need to investigate why that was.”Anadolu//Getty ImagesOliver Bearman.Advertisement - Continue Reading BelowBearman continues Haas’ strong startHaas caught the eye pre-season with a solid and compliant package but a haul of 17 points from two grands prix is a return that has surely exceeded expectations. Oliver Bearman was excellent once more in China, picking up a point in the Sprint Race before taking fifth position in the grand prix. Bearman’s result came despite dropping outside of the top 10 on the opening lap when he had to avoid the spinning Red Bull of Isack Hadjar, but from there he picked off rivals, managed his strategy to perfection, and resisted the lingering threat from Alpine’s Pierre Gasly. The 20-year-old is now fifth in the Drivers’ Championship, with Haas a promising fourth position in the Teams’ battle. “We couldn’t have asked for more, and I just want to keep pushing like this now,” Bearman said.The point of frustration for Haas comes from the other side of the garage, with Esteban Ocon still yet to score in 2026. Ocon, running the alternative tire strategy, was in the hunt for points but clumsily clattered into Franco Colapinto shortly after the pit stop phase and was issued a costly time penalty. Ocon apologized, while Haas boss Ayao Komatsu also pointed out a slight delay in the box unnecessarily put Ocon behind Colapinto in the first place. Komatsu was nevertheless delighted with Bearman’s result.“I really believe we got that P5 absolutely on merit, and that doesn’t happen overnight,” Komatsu said. “That’s an accumulation of effort from previous years, the parallel development of cars last year, hitting shakedown, and we’re learning every day. I’m so proud to see the daily improvement this team is making together to understand the car and get the most out of these regulations.”U.K.-based Phillip Horton started covering Grands Prix while still at university and swiftly deemed that writing about Formula 1 and the behind-the-scenes machinations was much more engaging than reading centuries-old novels. Degree gained, he went on to cover the sport full-time from 2014 and is as intrigued and excited by the destinations Formula 1 visits during its lengthy annual world tour as the racing itself. Phillip joined Autoweek in 2021 and while he has just about learned to spell in American English he has yet to find anywhere in America that makes a proper cup of tea.Read full bio
